# xcelsior_instance (Resource)

A GPU instance, billed by the second from the account's wallet.

Created through a launch plan: `terraform plan` quotes the launch without creating anything and warns when it falls outside the token's spend envelope; `apply` creates the plan, has it approved (by the envelope, or by a person within the provider's `approval_timeout`) and executes it. Every argument except `wait_for_running` forces a new instance. SSH keys registered on the account (`xcelsior_ssh_key`) are installed in the instance.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "xcelsior_gpus" "rtx4090" {
  gpu_model = "RTX 4090"
}

resource "xcelsior_ssh_key" "me" {
  name       = "laptop"
  public_key = file("~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub")
}

resource "xcelsior_volume" "datasets" {
  name    = "datasets"
  size_gb = 200

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}

resource "xcelsior_instance" "train" {
  name         = "train-llm"
  gpu_model    = "RTX 4090"
  num_gpus     = 1
  pricing_mode = "spot"
  image        = "pytorch/pytorch:2.5.1-cuda12.4-cudnn9-runtime"
  volume_ids   = [xcelsior_volume.datasets.id]

  timeouts {
    create = "45m"
  }

  # Registered keys are installed at launch.
  depends_on = [xcelsior_ssh_key.me]
}

output "ssh" {
  value = "ssh -p ${xcelsior_instance.train.ssh_port} root@${xcelsior_instance.train.host_ip}"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `gpu_model` (String) GPU model to rent, as `data.xcelsior_gpus` or `data.xcelsior_pricing` lists it. The launch is priced from it.
- `name` (String) Instance name, 1 to 128 characters.

### Optional

- `command` (String) Command to run in the container.
- `encrypted_workspace` (Boolean)
- `exclusive_gpu` (Boolean)
- `exposed_ports` (List of Number)
- `git_repo` (String) Public `https://` repository cloned at boot.
- `image` (String) Container image to run. Omit for the platform default.
- `init_script` (String, Sensitive) Script run in the container at boot (at most 4096 characters, 15 second cap).
- `num_gpus` (Number) Number of GPUs, 1 to 64. Defaults to 1.
- `pricing_mode` (String) `on_demand` (the default) or `spot`. A spot instance can be preempted; Terraform then plans a new one.
- `tier` (String) Service tier. Omit for the standard tier.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `volume_ids` (List of String) Volumes to mount at launch (at most 16). To attach a volume to an instance that is already running, use `xcelsior_volume_attachment`.
- `wait_for_running` (Boolean) Wait, within the create timeout, until the instance is running. Defaults to true. When false, apply ends once the launch is queued.

### Read-Only

- `host_id` (String) Host the instance was placed on.
- `host_ip` (String) Address to connect to.
- `host_key_fingerprint` (String) SSH host key fingerprint, to pin in `known_hosts`.
- `id` (String) The instance (job) id.
- `launch_plan_id` (String) The launch plan this instance was created from.
- `rate_per_hour_micros` (Number) Billed rate per hour, in millionths of the account currency.
- `ssh_port` (Number) Public SSH port.
- `status` (String) Lifecycle status as the API reports it (`queued`, `running`, ...).

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# An instance is imported by its id.
terraform import xcelsior_instance.train <instance-id>
```
